languageModelTools.name: deckard_query
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search the workspace's Markdown notes and tasks with a Deckard query.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches the user's local Markdown notes and checklist tasks, as indexed by the Deckard extension, with a Deckard query, and returns the matching note sections and tasks with their workspace-relative paths, one-based lines, and headings; tasks include their state, due date, and priority. Use it to answer questions about the user's notes, projects, people, and to-dos. For example, 'open tasks for Atlas' is tag = #project/atlas AND task = open, and 'what is overdue' is task = open AND due < today. Conditions combine with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. Fields: tag (tag = #project/atlas; tag = #risk/* matches a namespace; a bare #tag or @person also works), text (text ~ "vendor" matches words in note and task text), task (open, done, or any; only tasks match), due, scheduled, and start (a date such as 2026-09-20, today, tomorrow, a window such as 7d counted forward, or none), done (done = 7d means completed in the last seven days), priority (highest, high, medium, none, low, lowest; priority >= high), kind (an entity namespace such as project or person), file and path (with * and ? wildcards), created and updated (dates or windows such as 30d). Operators are = != ~ !~ > >= < <=. If you do not know a tag's exact name, call deckard_list_tags first.

query.description: A Deckard query, such as tag = #project/atlas AND task = open.

limit.description: The most notes, and the most tasks, to return. Defaults to 25; totals always count every match.

sort.description: Order by title, or newest created or updated first. Otherwise tasks are listed open first and soonest due first.

languageModelTools.name: deckard_list_tags
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the tags used in the workspace's Markdown notes, most used first.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the tags in the user's local Markdown notes, as indexed by the Deckard extension, most used first, with how many entries use each. Tags look like #project/atlas, #topic/leadership, or @person-name. Use it to find the exact tag to pass to deckard_query, optionally narrowed by a search such as 'atlas' or 'project/'.

search.description: Only tags whose name contains this text, such as atlas or project/.

limit.description: The most tags to return. Defaults to 50.

deckard.notesFolder.description: Optional workspace-relative folder containing Markdown notes. Leave empty to index all Markdown files in the workspace.

enumDescriptions: A dark technical operations interface inspired by the Oblivion reference screens.
A warm, high-contrast interface inspired by LCARS from Star Trek: The Next Generation.
A neon grid interface inspired by 1980s synthwave and outrun aesthetics.
A flight-display interface inspired by F-14 Tomcat HUD instrumentation.
A woodland travel-journal interface inspired by The Lord of the Rings.
deckard.theme.description: Visual theme used by Deckard webviews.

deckard.dashboard.openOnStartup.description: Open the Deckard Dashboard when VS Code starts in a workspace with indexed notes.

deckard.dailyNoteTemplate.description: Template used when creating a daily note.

deckard.templatesFolder.description: Folder of note templates, relative to the workspace folder. Deckard: New Note from Template lists its Markdown files, and Deckard does not index them. Leave it empty to turn templates off.

deckard.parseInlineTags.description: Index tags on non-heading Markdown lines as standalone entries.

deckard.personMarker.description: Single-character marker for people. For example, set this to "~" to recognize ~mara-vale as a person.

deckard.entityNamespaceAliases.description: Maps one #namespace to another. Targets can be built-in or custom; for example, { "proj": "project", "leadership": "management" } treats #proj/atlas as a project and collapses #leadership/performance into #management/performance.

deckard.enableTagAutocomplete.description: Show indexed tag suggestions after a tag or people marker. Disable without affecting tag indexing, highlighting, or navigation.

enumDescriptions: Keep tags in related-note and tag-overview titles.
Remove tags from titles and show them as separate tag controls.
deckard.tagTitleDisplayMode.description: Choose whether tags stay inline in note titles or appear separately.

deckard.tagOverview.hubNoteExpanded.description: Show a tag's hub note open at the top of its Tag Overview. When off, the hub starts collapsed to its title row; select the title to open it.

deckard.enableHeadingTagRelationships.description: Show weighted tag associations from explicit co-occurrence and heading proximity in Tag Overviews.

deckard.highlightNoteSections.description: Highlight indexed tagged note sections in Markdown editors.

deckard.editor.referenceCounts.description: Show, above the lines of a Markdown note, how many notes link to it, how many links name each heading, how many open tasks sit under each heading, and how many related entries Related Notes finds for each tagged heading.

deckard.editor.hoverPreviews.description: Preview the note or section a [[Wiki link]] points at when hovering it, and summarize a tag's entries when hovering the tag.

deckard.editor.linkDiagnostics.description: Mark a [[Wiki link]] that opens no note, because no note has its name or several do, and offer to create a missing note.

deckard.autoSelectNoteSections.description: Automatically show Related Notes for the tagged note section containing the cursor.

deckard.enableKeywordLinks.description: Let capped, section-scoped similarity of wording adjust the score of a related note that already shares a tag, association, or Wiki link. Shared wording never makes a note related on its own. Disable to rank by tags and links alone.

deckard.relatedNotesAssociationMinimumSu.description: Minimum distinct atomic source units required before a learned tag association affects Related Notes. One preserves intentional one-off associations.

deckard.relatedNotesRecencyHalfLifeDays.description: Optional Related Notes recency tie-breaker half-life in days. Zero disables it; daily-note and front-matter dates are preferred over filesystem dates.

deckard.tasks.addDoneDate.description: Add a completion date (✅ or [completion:: …]) when Deckard completes a task. Reopening the task removes it.

enumDescriptions: Obsidian Tasks emoji format, such as 📅 2026-09-20 ⏫ 🔁 every week.
Obsidian Tasks Dataview format, such as [due:: 2026-09-20] [priority:: high] [repeat:: every week].
deckard.tasks.metadataFormat.description: Format Deckard writes for a task that has no metadata yet, in / suggestions and completion dates. A task that already uses one format keeps it, and Deckard reads both.

deckard.tasks.metadataSuggestions.description: Suggest due dates, priorities, repeat rules, and dependencies after typing / in a task.

deckard.agenda.upcomingDays.description: How many days ahead the Agenda's Upcoming group looks for due, scheduled, and start dates.

deckard.board.statuses.description: Status columns on the task board, in order. A status found on a task but not listed here gets a column after them.

deckard.board.statusNamespace.description: Tag namespace that holds a task's status on the task board, so the default reads #status/doing.

deckard.outline.showTags.description: Show each heading's tags beside it in the Deckard Outline.

deckard.outline.followCursor.description: Select the Deckard Outline heading that contains the editor cursor.

deckard.outline.inheritedTags.description: Also show front-matter tags that every heading in the file inherits.

deckard.assistantTools.description: Let AI assistants in VS Code that use language model tools, such as GitHub Copilot in agent mode, search your notes and tasks with Deckard queries and list your tags. Deckard sends nothing anywhere itself; what a tool returns goes to the assistant that called it, which may send it to its own model service. VS Code asks you to allow the first call in each session.
